transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Raza (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Kapoor (Head of ML - IronClad), Evan Torres (CTO), Sana Ahmed (Product), Jordan Lee (SRE)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: scoping call for a 6-week pilot focused on retrieval-augmented support answers. Primary goals: define success metrics, agree on golden prompts and regression tests, size workload and pick benchmark targets, confirm security and deployment constraints.
Topics: success criteria, golden prompts, hallucination detection, format checks, scoring approach, load/latency targets, timeline.
Action items: see metadata list above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. This is Maya from Redwood. We also have Omar, our solutions engineer. Hey Omar.
[00:06] Omar Raza: Hi all, hi. Good to meet you folks.
[00:10] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Thanks, Maya. Long time planning to get to this, excited.
[00:15] Evan Torres: Same, trying to nail down the pilot scope quickly. We have compliance window late Sep so timeline matters.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great, quick agenda: confirm IronClad's success criteria, what a "golden" prompt set looks like for you, how you'd like us to run regressions and hallucination checks, and then load and latency targets plus timeline. Does that work?
[00:32] Sana Ahmed: Yes that sounds good. Also we'll need a quick note about availability for our infra folks for VPC peering.
[00:36] Jordan Lee: I'll be the point for SRE questions.

[01:10] Omar Raza: Before we get into prompts I want to call out our usual eval surfaces: we run a golden set for quality scoring (BLEU-like for structured output or human-labeled correctness for free-text), a regression suite (previously validated examples), and hallucination detectors (entity hallucination checks + factual cross-checks). We can also run format validators for JSON or templates.
[01:36] Dr. Priya Kapoor: For us, primary metric is correctness of customer-facing answers — precision over recall. We need >92% acceptable responses on golden set, and hallucination rate below 2% on a 95% CI. If those aren't met we won't push further.
[01:52] Evan Torres: And latency — 95th percentile <500 ms for single-turn support queries; our web UX expects sub-second. Cost is secondary but still important.

[03:05] Maya Chen: Helpful. Let's define data we'll use: Priya, you mentioned a tranche of anonymized queries?
[03:12] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Yes, we can provide 200 anonymized, high-quality customer queries plus about 400 edge-case prompts — some intentionally adversarial. We'll tag expected intents and preferred formats.
[03:24] Omar Raza: Perfect — we'll use 200 for golden set, 200 for regression and 400 for robustness/hallucination stress tests. For scoring, we propose hybrid: automatic scoring for format + simple metrics, then human review for borderline cases.

[04:05] Sana Ahmed: Walk me through how you detect hallucinations. We need reproducible checks because legal and ops will ask for auditability.
[04:12] Omar Raza: Sure. Two layers: first, token-level heuristics — e.g., presence of unsupported entities, numerical inconsistencies — then lightweight fact-checking against your canonical sources using RAG (retrieval) with top-k evidence scoring. We label outputs as factual, unsupported, or fabricated. We'll provide logs with evidence links for audit.
[04:35] Jordan Lee: Are those evidence links persisted? We need them in audit logs and they must be immutable w.r.t. TTL.
[04:40] Omar Raza: Yes, we can persist evidence IDs and include references in the transcript logs. If you're on Private or Dedicated we can also hook to your HSM-backed KMS for keying.

[05:30] (crosstalk)
[05:32] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Quick Q: for the golden prompts, are those single-turn or multi-turn?
[05:36] Omar Raza: Good q. We recommend a mix: 70% single-turn canonical queries, 30% multi-turn flows for stateful behavior and slot-filling format checks. We'll capture KV cache behavior for the multi-turns.

[06:10] Maya Chen: Timeline proposal: assume we sign pilot by next Friday, Redwood will provision a dedicated pilot environment (dedicated or private depending on contract). Week 0: onboarding and infra checks. Week 1-2: run baseline benchmarks and tune quantization. Week 3-4: run golden/regression and iterate. Week 5: final acceptance and handoff. Does that align with your compliance window?
[06:32] Evan Torres: That seems tight but workable. We need the security review done before week 2.
[06:36] Maya Chen: Understand. We'll include security packet — SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML docs — with the pilot proposal.

[08:00] Omar Raza: On benchmarks — we need to agree on workloads. Priya, what’s your expected QPS for peak?
[08:07] Dr. Priya Kapoor: For customer support we see bursts up to 40 qps but average is 6-8 qps. Most queries are short (avg 45 tokens), but some retrieval-enhanced ones go to 150 tokens.
[08:20] Omar Raza: We'll size for burst 50 qps to be safe. For latency targets, our goal is P95 < 500ms for short queries on dedicated capacity; if you want private/on-prem numbers we can run local perf tests.
[08:33] Jordan Lee: If we're on VPC peering, 95th may creep up depending on routing, so we should run end-to-end tests from your region.

[09:10] Sana Ahmed: Scoring approach — will you surface a single acceptance score or breakdowns?
[09:15] Omar Raza: Breakdown. Each case gets: format_score, factual_score, completeness_score, and human_override. We'll compute weighted aggregate per your weights — default is 40% factual, 30% completeness, 20% format, 10% latency/cost penalty. You can adjust weights for the pilot.
[09:32] Dr. Priya Kapoor: We need factual at 50% weight, since wrong facts are unacceptable. So let's set factual 50, completeness 25, format 15, latency/cost 10.
[09:42] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll run with that weighting for acceptance criteria and show per-case breakdowns in the dashboard.

[11:05] Evan Torres: On formats — many of our outputs must be strict JSON with a fixed schema for downstream processing. Does Redwood do strict schema validation?
[11:12] Omar Raza: Yes, we can run JSON schema validation and fail cases that don't conform. Those count towards format_score. We can also run sanitizers to coerce minor issues but we'll flag them.
[11:24] Dr. Priya Kapoor: We expect fewer than 1% schema fails on golden set.

[12:40] Maya Chen: Let's talk regression cadence. We propose: daily smoke runs on baseline, weekly full regression during pilot, and ad-hoc runs after any model changes. Do you want us to gate deployments on regression pass thresholds?
[12:52] Evan Torres: Yes. Any rollout to prod should be gated. For pilot, we'll require 95% pass on the golden set before we'd consider production rollout.

[14:00] Omar Raza: About model variants: we'll suggest a primary model (open quantized) plus a fallback that trades accuracy for latency. Smart routing can route to fallback when load spikes. That preserves availability.
[14:12] Jordan Lee: If fallback is used we need telemetry in our console to show % of traffic and degrade gracefully.
[14:18] Omar Raza: Absolutely — we'll add route-level telemetry and alerting thresholds.

[15:30] (minor audio dropout at ~15:45)
[15:40] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Security Q: our legal team insists on KMS separation and key custody for logs. Can Redwood accommodate customer-managed keys?
[15:47] Maya Chen: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS; HSM integrations are possible in on-prem packages. We'll add that to the security addendum.

[17:00] Sana Ahmed: On evaluation — for borderline outputs that fail automatic scoring, will Redwood provide a UI for humans to adjudicate?
[17:07] Omar Raza: We have a review UI where your annotators can mark outputs as Pass/Fail and supply notes. Those labels feed back into regression sets.

[18:40] Dr. Priya Kapoor: A tricky part: hallucinations that include made-up policy numbers or dates can be subtle. How do you surface those?
[18:48] Omar Raza: We'll run entity-level matching against your canonical dataset (policy ids, product SKUs). If an entity isn't found in top-k retrieval results, we flag it. For ambiguous IDs we present candidate evidence items for human review.

[20:10] Maya Chen: Let's document acceptance gates explicitly so legal can see them. Draft acceptance: 1) Weighted quality score >= threshold (we'll compute sample), 2) Hallucination rate <=2%, 3) Schema failure <=1%, 4) P95 latency <=500ms on short queries, 5) Security checklist signed. If any fail, the pilot enters remediation for 2 weeks. Agreed?
[20:34] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Agreed for pilot gating.

[22:00] Evan Torres: Pricing question — what's the delta if we choose Dedicated pilot vs Hosted? We may want dedicated to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
[22:08] Maya Chen: Dedicated has higher baseline commit but gives stable P95 and capacity guarantees. For 6-week pilot we can offer a short-term reserved pool discount; I'll include numbers in the proposal.

[24:20] Sana Ahmed: For regression tests, how do you handle prompt drift and updates to golden set?
[24:26] Omar Raza: We'll version the golden set and have a change-log. Any change requires a retained snapshot and re-run of regression to show impact. We can also tag examples as "must pass" which are blockers.

[26:40] Jordan Lee: On infra prep — I'll need a checklist: CIDR ranges, peering windows, KMS endpoints, and service account details.
[26:47] Maya Chen: We'll send a one-pager infra checklist.

[28:05] Dr. Priya Kapoor: One more on scoring: can we get example scorecards after a run? We want CSVs per-case for downstream analysis.
[28:13] Omar Raza: Yes, CSV and JSONL exports with per-case breakdown and evidence links. We'll include human labels and versioning metadata.

[30:00] Maya Chen: Let's surface a sample run briefly — Omar, can you summarize what the first baseline run will show?
[30:08] Omar Raza: Baseline will be: throughput run at avg 8 qps, peak 50 qps with simulated network; a golden-set pass where we run the 200 curated prompts and compute weighted score; hallucination run where we inject adversarial prompts; and a schema validation sweep. Expected deliverables: dashboard, per-case CSV, and a regression snapshot.

[32:20] (brief pause)
[32:30] Dr. Priya Kapoor: About the golden prompts — we'll include high-priority customer-friction examples and a few internal examples that mimic policy lookups. We want those locked once sent.
[32:40] Omar Raza: Good. Locking is fine. We'll only accept changes via the change-log process.

[34:00] Evan Torres: What about human-in-the-loop? We might want to approve certain high-risk responses before they go live.
[34:07] Omar Raza: We can add a moderation queue where outputs flagged by low confidence or high novelty go to a reviewer before being returned. That has latency implications but works for high-risk flows.

[36:10] Sana Ahmed: Can you also include cost telemetry per route so product can see unit economics?
[36:15] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdowns per-route and per-model. We'll expose that in the pilot.

[38:00] Jordan Lee: For audit logs, retention policy? We need 1 year for our compliance.
[38:06] Maya Chen: We can set retention; for hosted modes there may be extra cost for long-term retention. For Private deployments you control retention.

[40:20] (short side conversation about calendar)
[41:05] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Quick check — do you have any example hallucination reports?
[41:10] Omar Raza: Yes I'll upload a sample PDF with flagged examples and evidence for last pilot.

[42:30] Maya Chen: Ok, to recap concrete next steps: (1) Redwood to send pilot proposal + pricing + security packet by 2026-08-14; (2) Omar to deliver benchmark harness + golden prompts template by 2026-08-13; (3) IronClad to provide anonymized datasets and infra answers by 2026-08-16; (4) schedule infra kickoff 2026-08-17. Anything to add?
[42:55] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Please include acceptance gates and remediation plan in the proposal.
[43:00] Maya Chen: Will do.

[45:00] (wrap-up)
[45:10] Evan Torres: Thanks all. If we can get the docs early next week we can slot this into our compliance window.
[45:18] Maya Chen: Great, we'll follow up today with calendar invites and the doc links.
[45:24] Sana Ahmed: Thanks.
[45:26] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone.
[45:30] (meeting end)

Notes on transcript authenticity: minor mis-transcriptions present in original audio (e.g., "KV cache" appears as "K V cache" in some segments; some names auto-labeled as Speaker 2). Some filler words removed for readability but timing preserved.

References mentioned: security packet (SOC 2/ISO/SSO), benchmarking harness (link to be provided), golden prompt template (to be provided).
